blocks.label: after his win over Jodar
blocks.text: I knew it wasn't going to be an easy match going in. I was happy that I was able to get through some tough moments in the first set, early when I was down break points, to be able to hold serve and get to that tiebreaker. Once I was in the tiebreaker I felt confident, fending off those set points and coming through it in the end. It was a tricky second set as well, being up a break and losing it, but I thought I fought well and competed well.

blocks.label: on his semi-final hopes and the Fritz–Zverev match
blocks.text: I'm looking forward to it either way. I think both those guys are great guys. I'd love to make the semi-finals here for the first time. I did my job today and let's see what happens. I'm always rooting for him. I think him and Sasha are going to have a great match. I think if he takes Sasha out in straights, he gets through to the semi-finals.

blocks.label: on Jodar's rookie-year qualification for Turin
blocks.text: Rafa is one of the best young talents that tennis has seen in a long time. To be here playing in Turin in his first year on tour, starting the year outside of the top 100, is a ridiculous feat. So I hope all you guys recognize how special that is.

blocks.label: on his aggressive game and return mindset
blocks.text: I'm trying to be smart in the decisions I make. I still play very aggressively. I pay attention above all to my footwork and I try to take the ball early. I think that when I manage to win the long rallies and come out of them without making wrong decisions or committing unforced errors, that's where opponents struggle the most against me. When I step on court, everyone knows I have a big serve. But if opponents think: Ok, I just have to get a few balls back in play and then Ben will miss, it becomes much easier for them to take control and feel comfortable in the rally. When instead the opponent feels he has to do something special to beat me, with the way I'm able to move and cover the court now, which is much better than before, it becomes harder for him to find solutions. So I try to stay true to my identity, play aggressively and come to the net when I can, all this without falling apart from the baseline. It's not a tournament where you arrive and immediately feel at ease. This year I changed my mindset on the return.

blocks.label: on his season
blocks.text: Either way, it's been an incredible year for me. I'm happy with the way I competed throughout the year, the way I've bounced back after difficult things have happened, and to win two matches here after making a deep run in Paris as well, I feel that I put a positive end to my season.

blocks.label: on bringing Juan Carlos Ferrero into his team
blocks.text: The reason that we brought him on is for a different philosophy from the tennis perspective, the experience that he has from a coaching perspective and a playing perspective. I think there are so many improvements I can make on the other surfaces, with my groundstrokes, technically, strategically as well. From what I can see in a small amount of time, I think it'll work very well. I think the great thing is that, outside of a tennis perspective, the philosophy is similar in how they approach the game, the type of people they are. With the little amount of time I've spent with Juan Carlos, things have become pretty clear: the type of guy he is, the character that he has, the non-negotiables in terms of attitude. There are so many things that go hand in hand with my dad as well. So that part is easy.

blocks.label: after his win over Fils
blocks.text: I thought the first two matches were very, very high level. Today I thought I played a little bit worse from the baseline, but I'm very happy to have won all three matches against three very difficult opponents. I'm happy to be through in straight sets.

blocks.label: on his recurring ankle pain
blocks.text: Unfortunately, I started feeling my ankle again. I'll probably feel my ankle sometimes until the end of my career. It's unfortunately the injury that I had, it's quite big. Every once in a while, it happens like that. There is no particular reason why it happens. There is nothing like a single movement that makes it go. I'm going to do everything I can to be pain-free on Saturday, but this is something that I have to live with nowadays. I hope I'll be 100 percent on Saturday.

blocks.label: on how the ankle affects his serve
blocks.text: On the serve more than on the baseline, because I feel like I can still move well. But you can see immediately my serve speed goes down, my percentage goes down when that happens.

blocks.label: on playing Fils
blocks.text: Arthur for me personally is a very difficult opponent as well because of how much power he has.

latest.text:
Zverev beat Fils 6–4, 7–6 in the group stage to finish his group with six sets won out of six, still without losing his serve all week. It was the first appearance of Fils at this event and Zverev had already won the McEnroe group before the match.

The first set turned on a single break. Zverev broke for 4–3 and held on from there to take it 6–4. The second set had no break of serve and Fils came closest when Zverev served at 5–6. He had two set points and Zverev saved both. That was the moment of the match. The tiebreak ran long, with five points in a row saved, before Zverev took it 8–6. Zverev knows his level dropped a little: "Today I thought I played a little bit worse from the baseline, but I'm very happy to have won all three matches, against three very difficult opponents, …"

Even on a lesser day, he found answers. He hit several well-struck passing shots, a fine backhand among them and finished points well around the net. Zverev was at his best when it mattered most. He saved every break point he faced, while Fils could not and he won 83% of the points behind his first serve.

A very good group stage from Zverev, clean from start to finish in these fast indoor conditions. He was happy to be through in straight sets and with no break conceded all week he had every reason to be. Medvedev or Tiafoe waits in the semi-finals.

The first set went to a tiebreak, which Shelton won 10-8 after he survived a chance for Jodar late in the breaker and his backhand held up well toward the end. Jodar produced some strong returns, including a very deep one off a fast second serve into his forehand that left Shelton little to do. After the tiebreak Shelton held serve well, hitting the ball aggressively to big deep targets and he kept hurting Jodar, at one point leaving him almost on the ground. The win gave Shelton two wins out of three in the group but his place in the semi-finals was not yet guaranteed and depended on the evening match.

composed.body:
Shelton beat Jodar 7–6, 7–5 in the group stage to move closer to the semi-finals, though his place there was not yet guaranteed. It was Jodar's first appearance at this event.

The first set had no break. Shelton saved 2 break points early on and the set went to a long tiebreak. Jodar had a chance late in it but Shelton held on and took it 10–8 to lead by a set. In the second set he broke first, before Jodar broke back to level at 4–4. Shelton afterwards: "a tricky second set as well being up a break and losing it But I thought I fought well competed well" He broke again for 6–5 and served out the match.

That late break showed where he won it. His return was the base of it all: he won 66% of the points against the second serve, far above his usual 48%. It was not a clean match from him, with 32 unforced errors and just 57% of first serves in against his 69% average.

Late in the second set Jodar called the physio, his second medical timeout in two matches.

All in all, very little separated them and Shelton was the stronger player on the few points that mattered. Next is his last group match.
